greek: Ὤφθη δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ θεὸς πρὸς τῇ δρυὶ τῇ Μαμβρη καθημένου αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς θύρας τῆς σκηνῆς αὐτοῦ μεσημβρίας.
hint: God appears to Abraham by the oak of Mamre as he sits at his tent door at noon.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *YHWH*. The Greek has ὁ θεός.
The genitive absolute: the participle's `of` stands before each gloss, as the case's does for a noun.
The genitive of time; μεσημβρία is first *mid-day, noon*.
The repeated article before the name, plain `the`, as at 14:13.

greek: ἀναβλέψας δὲ τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς αὐτοῦ εἶδεν, καὶ ἰδοὺ τρεῖς ἄνδρες εἱστήκεισαν ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἰδὼν προσέδραμεν εἰς συνάντησιν αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ τῆς θύρας τῆς σκηνῆς αὐτοῦ καὶ προσεκύνησεν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν
hint: He looks up: three men stand over him; he runs to meet them and bows to the ground.

notes.text: The pluperfect of ἵστημι, whose perfect and pluperfect take the intransitive senses, *to be set, placed, to stand*: `had been set and stood so`.
συνάντησις, one translation, *a meeting*: plain text, as at 14:17.
προσκυνέω is first *to make obeisance*, then *fall down and worship*; its second sense, *making the salam, prostrating oneself before*, follows in the aorist.
Rahlfs prints no punctuation at the end of the verse.

hint: Lord, if I have found favour in your sight, do not pass by your servant.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾădōnāy*. The Greek has the vocative of κύριος, singular, to three men.
Perseus keys ἄρα with a rough breathing; its first sense, *then, straightway, at once*, heads.

Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

hint: Let water be brought to wash your feet, and rest under the tree.

notes.text: Middle Liddell files νίπτω under νίζω, first *to wash the hands* or *feet* of another: *feet* is no gloss by itself, and *to wash the hands* heads. Nothing names who washes; the verb is third plural.

δένδρον, one translation, *a tree*: plain text. Not δρῦς, whose headword at 18:1 is also *the tree*.
δή, the chain of GEN 15:5.

greek: καὶ ἔσπευσεν Αβρααμ ἐπὶ τὴν σκηνὴν πρὸς Σαρραν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Σπεῦσον καὶ φύρασον τρία μέτρα σεμιδάλεως καὶ ποίησον ἐγκρυφίας.
hint: Abraham hurries to Sarah: quick, knead three measures of fine flour and make cakes.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *šĕlōš sĕʾîm qemaḥ sōlet*, *three seahs of flour, fine flour*. The Greek has *three measures of the finest wheaten flour*.
σπεύδω is first *to set a-going, to urge on, hasten*; its intransitive *to press on, hasten* follows in its own voice.
One translation each: *the finest wheaten flour*, *baked in the ashes*: plain text.
φυράω is *to mix* flour *so as to make* it *into dough, to knead*: the pieces between are no glosses by themselves.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: καὶ εἰς τὰς βόας ἔδραμεν Αβρααμ καὶ ἔλαβεν μοσχάριον ἁπαλὸν καὶ καλὸν καὶ ἔδωκεν τῷ παιδί, καὶ ἐτάχυνεν τοῦ ποιῆσαι αὐτό.
hint: He runs to the herd, takes a tender calf, and gives it to the servant to prepare.

notes.text: No Middle Liddell entry; LSJ, *little calf*, one translation: plain text.
The article before the infinitive is not printed, as at 2:5.
ταχύνω is first *to make quickly*; its intransitive *to be quick, to make haste* follows.

greek: εἶπεν δέ Ἐπαναστρέφων ἥξω πρὸς σὲ κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦτον εἰς ὥρας, καὶ ἕξει υἱὸν Σαρρα ἡ γυνή σου. Σαρρα δὲ ἤκουσεν πρὸς τῇ θύρᾳ τῆς σκηνῆς, οὖσα ὄπισθεν αὐτοῦ.
hint: I will come back to you at this time next year, and Sarah will have a son. Sarah hears at the tent door.

notes.lemma: κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦτον … καὶ ἕξει υἱὸν Σαρρα
notes.text: Paul quotes the promise as κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦτον ἐλεύσομαι καὶ ἔσται τῇ Σάρρᾳ υἱός, Romans 9:9, joining this verse to 18:14.

notes.lemma: κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦτον εἰς ὥρας
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *kāʿēt ḥayyâ*, *at the time of life*, of the coming year. The Greek has *at this time, into seasons*.
ὥρα is first *period*, of year, month or day; the plural takes each sense in the plural, *Hours* capitalised as the lexicon prints the goddesses.
ἥκω, whose present is a perfect, *has come*, as at 6:13: the future, `I will have come`.

Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: Αβρααμ δὲ καὶ Σαρρα πρεσβύτεροι προβεβηκότες ἡμερῶν, ἐξέλιπεν δὲ Σαρρα γίνεσθαι τὰ γυναικεῖα.
hint: Abraham and Sarah are old, far on in days; Sarah no longer has the way of women.

notes.text: Middle Liddell files the comparative inside πρέσβυς: *elder, older*, and, in the New Testament, *an elder of the Jewish Council*, *an elder of the Church, presbyter*. The word MorphGNT files under itself.
The perfect participle of προβαίνω, *to step on, step forward, advance*: `having stepped on and standing so`.

γυναικεῖος is first *of* or *belonging to women*; *of* is no gloss by itself. Its noun sense, *the women's apartments*, is the singular τὸ γυναικεῖον's, so the article and the adjective's senses stand, as ὁ οἰκογενής is `the born in the house`.
ἐκλείπω, the chain of GEN 8:13, with the present infinitive of γίνομαι.

notes.lemma: Οὔπω μέν μοι γέγονεν ἕως τοῦ νῦν

The adverb, filed inside ἀληθής: *truly*, then *really, actually, in reality*.
The perfect of γηράσκω, *to grow old, become old*; the causal *to bring to old age* is the aorist's alone.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take them for a proper name.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Μή τι, κύριε, ἐὰν λαλήσω ἔτι ἅπαξ· ἐὰν δὲ εὑρεθῶσιν ἐκεῖ δέκα; καὶ εἶπεν Οὐ μὴ ἀπολέσω ἕνεκεν τῶν δέκα.
hint: Let me speak once more: suppose ten? I will not destroy it for the ten.

notes.text: Middle Liddell, one sense, *once, once only, once for all*.

greek: ἀπῆλθεν δὲ κύριος, ὡς ἐπαύσατο λαλῶν τῷ Αβρααμ, καὶ Αβρααμ ἀπέστρεψεν εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτοῦ.
hint: The Lord goes away when he has finished speaking with Abraham, and Abraham returns to his place.

notes.text: The middle of παύω with the participle, the chain of GEN 11:8, singular.
ἀποστρέφω, the chain of GEN 3:19, in the aorist, with *himself* for the lexicon's *oneself*.
